items.statement: Catheter failure among catheters inserted in the 12 months after the policy change is no more than 3 percentage points higher than in the 12 months before, after accounting for several catheters per patient and pre-existing trends.
items.rationale: The need is high because the executive may reverse the policy; retrieved comparisons found little change in failure (claims c1 and c3), so the question is whether a meaningful local rise can be ruled out; the data exist.
items.risks: Secular change between the two years, and removal reasons recorded differently between periods.

items.statement: The policy reduced the number of catheters per admission by at least 20 percent.
items.rationale: Fewer insertions is the expected benefit and the one patients notice.
items.risks: Length of stay may have changed between the periods.

items.statement: Failure after the change is concentrated in catheters with gaps in site assessment documentation.
items.rationale: Incomplete documentation was linked with infiltration elsewhere (claim c2).
items.risks: Documentation gaps may mark sicker patients rather than missed assessments.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the decision-relevant question, with insertions per admission as the main secondary question.
